idiom_name: frozen @dataclass operations + match statement with class patterns
implementation_notes: Frozen dataclasses model the operations; annotated as `Get | Put | Log` they read as an ADT, and the interpreter is a `match` statement whose class patterns deconstruct and dispatch in one construct - the visitor and `__match_args__` boilerplate disappear. `match` is not closed: an unmatched statement falls through silently, so the interpreter must end with `case _: raise TypeError(...)`, and typing offers no exhaustiveness either - a totality test over the algebra belongs in the suite. The classic class-per-node-with-`interpret` form is still justified when nodes genuinely own behaviour and third-party subclassing is expected; otherwise the data-plus-match shape is the shorter Python.
pitfalls: An unmatched `match` falls through silently, so always end with `case _: raise TypeError(...)` and a test that walks every operation.
`frozen=True` is what makes programs values: without it an interpreter can mutate the program and equality-based assertions get fragile.
Dataclass equality recurses into all fields, and unhashable fields (list/dict) make programs unusable as dict keys; deep programs are expensive to compare.

variants.name: functools.singledispatch generic-function interpreter
variants.idiom_name: @singledispatch run(op) with one registered function per operation
variants.implementation_notes: Instead of one `match` statement, each operation gets a registered implementation (`@run.register`) so a new interpreter is a new dispatch chain and libraries can extend the algebra by registering handlers for their own node types - the open, generic-function flavour of the same pattern. This is the floor-safe form on Python 3.4-3.9 (no match statement) and suits pluggable interpreter registries; the price is that the operation set is open, no tool lists the covered cases, and the registry grows by import side effect, so totality needs an explicit check.
pitfalls: singledispatch matches the first argument's class MRO-style: a handler registered for a base class can shadow a more specific one.
The registry is global and populated by import side effects: a handler module that is never imported silently changes behaviour after deployment.
Registered functions share the name `run`, so debuggers and tracebacks show `_` for every handler unless they are named explicitly.
